stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The mention of Llama-3.1 indicates ongoing development and community interest in Meta's latest LLMs.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformer, llama, and AI/ML communities.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Major music publishers (Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell) are suing AI company Anthropic.
The lawsuit alleges copyright infringement concerning tens of thousands of copyrighted musical works.
The financial stakes are high, with potential damages reaching up to $150,000 per infringed work.

stories.title: CLAP: Cross-Embodiment Video World Models are Zero-Shot Physical Simulators
stories.author: Ola Shorinwa
bullet_points: Introduces CLAP, a new framework for cross-embodiment action-conditioned video generation.
Addresses the limitation of current models being restricted to a single robot embodiment.
Enables training on diverse, internet-scale videos (human and robotic) to learn generalizable physics.

stories.title: Token-Level Advertising
stories.author: Qi Qi
bullet_points: Proposes Latent Advertiser Mixture Auction (LAMA), a new advertising mechanism for generative AI.
Shifts advertising from traditional predefined slots to a generation-native, token-level approach.
Advertisers influence the generation process by reporting local continuation values that guide next-token policies.

stories.title: Arbitrary code execution in QubesOS via copy-to-VM error reporting backchannel
stories.author: vntok
bullet_points: A critical vulnerability (Arbitrary Code Execution) was discovered in QubesOS.
The vulnerability stems from an error reporting backchannel related to copy-to-VM operations.
This represents a significant security flaw in a major security-focused operating system.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a generative AI.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the current LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for persistent AI agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It emphasizes running complex agent workflows locally on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and 8VC.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also delivers faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new large language model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents entirely on local, personal hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
This integration specifically targets and optimizes performance on Apple Silicon hardware.
The feature is currently available in a preview release, indicating ongoing development.

stories.title: Inside Meta’s push to put robots to work in data centers
stories.author: Paresh Dave, WIRED.com
bullet_points: Meta is actively piloting the use of robotics within its data centers.
The robots are being tested to automate tasks currently performed by human technicians.
This signals a significant industry trend toward advanced automation in large-scale infrastructure.

stories.title: Trump blacklisting of "woke" Anthropic deemed illegal by federal judge
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A federal judge ruled that Trump's blacklisting of Anthropic based on its stance against 'woke' policies was illegal.
Anthropic has publicly opposed the development of lethal autonomous warfare and mass surveillance technologies.
The ruling highlights legal challenges surrounding government actions targeting AI companies based on their ethical stances.

stories.title: RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution
stories.author: Haoliang Li
bullet_points: Introduces RedEvoAgent, an automatic red-teaming agent designed to evolve its skills based on experience.
Highlights the increased risk posed by LLM agents in production environments due to potential harmful tool use and state changes, beyond simple text generation.
Addresses limitations in existing red-teaming methods, specifically the risk of retrieval bias in trajectory-based attack retrieval.

stories.title: CorporateBench: Large-Scale Q&A Benchmarking with Temporal Knowledge Bases
stories.author: Igor Labutov
bullet_points: Introduces CorporateBench (CB), a large-scale, human-validated Q&A benchmark designed for enterprise-scale document collections.
Addresses the critical evaluation challenge in corporate LLM applications where proprietary data sharing is restricted and synthetic data is insufficient.
CB evaluates LLMs across multiple tasks using a corpus exceeding 230,000 documents, simulating real-world corporate communication complexity.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services (Claude) with local, open-source LLM infrastructure (Ollama).

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine for better performance on Apple silicon devices.

stories.title: Musicians-turned-detectives are hunting for AI grifters
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Sophisticated generative audio tools are leading to the proliferation of AI-generated music.
This AI music often mimics the melodies and vocals of human artists.
The issue involves copyright and ethics, with some creators admitting to using AI while others deny it.

stories.title: I asked 100 companies for my data. Some deleted it instead.
stories.author: Reece Rodgers, wired.com
bullet_points: The article investigates the practical challenges of exercising data privacy rights.
Testing across 100 companies revealed significant confusion in handling data deletion requests.
The findings highlight systemic friction between user privacy demands and corporate data management practices.

stories.title: Meta makes AI glasses slightly less creepy with limit on nonconsensual recording
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta has implemented a safety feature in its AI glasses to prevent unauthorized recording.
The glasses will cease recording if the user covers the designated safety light.
This update addresses privacy concerns related to nonconsensual recording capabilities of the device.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile and persist specialized knowledge and workflows learned by AI agents.
It addresses the limitation where valuable insights from agent interaction remain scattered across optimization histories.
The system enables AI agents to progressively adapt and reuse learned skills across different iterations.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of using only successful trajectories for training LLMs to solve software issues.
Prior methods relying on large-scale agent trajectory datasets suffer from noisy supervision, as success doesn't guarantee quality.
SWE-Prime proposes a method to improve LLM performance by mitigating the risks associated with imitating suboptimal steps in successful trajectories.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Current LLM-based code review models often treat the process as a single, static decision.
Real-world code review is inherently iterative and interactive, involving multiple rounds of feedback.
The paper introduces MCR-Bench to benchmark LLMs against the complex, multi-round nature of realistic code review.

stories.title: Mechanistic Reaction Prediction via Discrete Flow Matching on Graph-Structured Electron Occupation
stories.author: Philippe Schwaller
bullet_points: Introduces MAELLE, a new method for predicting chemical reactions.
MAELLE models reactions not as molecule generation or graph edits, but as discrete flow matching over electron occupation vectors.
This approach addresses the limitation of current ML methods that treat reactions purely as topological or generative problems.

stories.title: Persona-Execution Separation: An Architecture Pattern for Evolving LLM Agents under Execution Audit
stories.author: Yisen Xi
bullet_points: Introduces Persona-Execution Separation (PES) as an architectural pattern for LLM agents.
Addresses the conflict between allowing LLM personas to evolve freely and maintaining auditable, traceable execution.
Proposes separating persona (which can drift) and execution (which must be faceless and audited) into distinct trust domains.

stories.title: Beyond F1: Evaluating Coverage and Failure Recovery in AI Model Security Scanners
stories.author: Indranil Sanyal
bullet_points: The research addresses limitations in current AI model security scanner evaluation, which often only measures successful judgments.
The study introduces a controlled benchmark using synthetic Pickle and PyTorch artifacts to test scanners like ModelScan and ModelAudit.
The evaluation covers 170 artifacts across 145 specimen families, providing a more comprehensive view of scanner coverage and failure recovery.

stories.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
stories.author: Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
bullet_points: Addresses the limitations of outdated, fixed-variable sepsis severity indices in modern critical care.
Introduces a novel machine learning approach to learn a continuous sepsis severity score directly from patient trajectories.
Validated through a retrospective study involving a large cohort of patients from two hospital systems.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: Research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) internally structure and organize moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs differentiate between specific moral foundations (e.g., care/harm, fairness).
The methodology involves training linear probes on open-weight models, mapping these foundations geometrically.

stories.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
stories.author: Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
bullet_points: Addresses the limitations of outdated, fixed-variable sepsis severity indices.
Proposes a novel machine learning approach to learn continuous sepsis severity scores directly from patient trajectories.
Validated through a retrospective study involving over 36,000 adult patients across two hospital systems.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) internally structure and organize moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs can differentiate between specific Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) categories.
Researchers use six independent linear probes, one for each MFT category, to geometrically analyze the organization within open-weight models.

stories.title: Puro-2B: Poor Lab's Qwen2-1.5B Trained on RTX 5090 within $5090
stories.author: Wenguang Chen
bullet_points: Addresses the high cost barrier in large language model (LLM) pretraining, a major hurdle for open-source and academic researchers.
Introduces 'Puro-2B,' a cost-efficient training recipe utilizing the RTX 5090 GPU.
Contrasts the new approach with the prohibitive costs of training established models like Llama-3.2-3B.

stories.title: Understanding Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning: Broader Reasoning Coverage than GRPO
stories.author: Zhenkun Wang
bullet_points: The paper investigates Evolution Strategies (ES) as a memory-efficient post-training method for improving LLM reasoning.
It systematically analyzes the optimization dynamics of ES to compare its performance against established methods like GRPO.
The research empirically and theoretically demonstrates that ES offers a performance advantage over GRPO in certain reasoning tasks.

stories.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
stories.author: Ting Zhu
bullet_points: Introduces CritICL, a novel inference-time framework designed to improve LLM reasoning.
Addresses the inefficiency of current methods (like repeated generation) by leveraging structured patterns in LLM failure modes across model scales.
Aims to enhance reasoning performance while maintaining high computational efficiency.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile and persist specialized knowledge and workflows from AI agent experiences.
It addresses the limitation where valuable insights guiding skill development are currently scattered across optimization histories.
The system enables AI agents to progressively adapt and reuse learned skills across multiple interactions.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of using only successful agent trajectories for training LLMs on software issues.
Prior methods suffer from noisy supervision because successful paths can still contain ineffective or risky steps.
The proposed SWE-Prime aims to improve LLM performance by refining the supervision process beyond simple trajectory collection.

stories.title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: The paper introduces TTPO (Test-Time Policy Optimization) to address limitations in post-training methods like RL and OPSD for LLMs.
Existing methods rely on ground-truth labels, which prevents effective test-time training (TTT).
TTPO proposes using majority-vote pseudo-labels as an alternative to ground truth, while analyzing the inherent fragility and asymmetry of this approach.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The paper addresses the limitation of current LLM-based code review systems, which treat the process as a single, static decision.
It introduces MCR-Bench to benchmark code review in a realistic, multi-round, and interactive manner.
The research aims to capture the complex, iterative problem-solving nature of real-world software development code reviews.

stories.title: Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR
stories.author: Dongyan Zhao
bullet_points: The research addresses a key limitation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for LLMs: entropy collapse leading to narrow reasoning coverage.
The proposed solution introduces cross-model non-parametric perturbation to maintain the generative diversity of LLMs during RLVR training.
This work offers an alternative to existing algorithmic regularizations to improve LLM performance (pass@$k$) without sacrificing exploration.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: Research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs differentiate between specific Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) categories.
The methodology involves training linear probes on open-weight models to map these moral foundations geometrically.

stories.title: Making Clinical Language Models Auditable: Concept-Guided Fine-Tuning for Robust Prediction
stories.author: Guanhua Chen
bullet_points: Clinical language models often fail in real-world deployment due to overfitting to note-specific artifacts (e.g., templates, boilerplate).
The paper introduces CAST (Concept-guided Artifact Suppression Tuning), an SAE-based framework to address this issue.
CAST uses Sparse Autoencoders to extract human-auditable features from Transformer activations, enabling more robust and auditable clinical text classification.

stories.title: I gave an AI agent a production rollback button — then spent the hackathon trying to trick it into pressing it
stories.author: prince_panchani_f971a20ec
bullet_points: The article explores the security implications of AI agents in production environments.
A minor configuration error (one-line omission) can bypass an AI agent's approval gate.
The piece uses a hackathon scenario to demonstrate the risks of over-reliance on AI safety mechanisms.
